title: The Colony of the Deep
premise: Dominic Whitlock, a clone of the murdered original, keeps the beacon that masks the colony from two rival fleets locked in a fragile truce. When the colony's children begin sharing a dream of a drowned city beneath the ice, they uncover the truth: the beacon isn't a warning system but a lie broadcast to both fleets, each believing the other holds the colony hostage. As the truce nears expiration and the children's dream reveals the original Whitlock's killer is still among them, Dominic must choose between exposing the truth—which could trigger war—and preserving the lie, which erases the colonists' identity forever. In the end, Dominic broadcasts the children's shared dream instead of the lie, forcing both fleets to confront the colony as real people; the fleets stand down, the killer surrenders, and the colony claims its own name at last.
about_author: Lena Montrose is the pen name of a former marine acoustics researcher who spent three years stationed in the Antarctic before turning to fiction. Her novels explore what survives of identity when memory can be copied, and she writes from a coastal cabin where the fog does most of her worldbuilding.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Already Dead
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He performs his morning maintenance on the beacon while reciting memories that aren't his—the original Whitlock's wedding, his murder. The colony treats him with polite distance. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness of being a copy nobody mourns.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Season
chapters.summary: POV: Mara, a twelve-year-old hydroponics apprentice. She wakes screaming from a dream of a drowned city and discovers four other children dreamed it identically, down to the street names. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Beacon Protocol
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He reviews the beacon's logs and finds transmissions he never authorized—old ones, predating his activation, signed by the original. Someone edited the archive. Emotional beat: first crack in his trust of the colony's founders.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The children sneak to the glacier shelf and find a hatch matching their dream. Beneath: a flooded pre-colony settlement, older than the official founding date. Emotional beat: thrill of discovery shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Council leader Ilsa Voss intercepts him and confesses partially: the beacon broadcasts fabricated fleet codes making each side believe the other controls the colony. The truce expires in ninety days. Emotional beat: dread of inherited responsibility.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Eleven children now share the dream, and it has begun to change—a door in the drowned city that was closed is now open. Adults dismiss them; Voss quietly orders the children monitored. Emotional beat: isolation of knowing something adults refuse to see.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Suspects
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Reopening the original's murder file, he narrows suspects to three colonists who arrived on the founding ship—including Voss herself. His investigation makes him a target; someone sabotages the beacon's coolant. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: The Door in the Water
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Diving with borrowed gear, the children enter the open door and find a chamber of stasis pods—one occupied, its occupant wearing the original Whitlock's face. Emotional beat: horror that the dream is not a memory but an invitation.

chapters.title: Truce Mathematics
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A scout drone from Fleet Kestrel penetrates the perimeter; the beacon barely deflects it. Dominic calculates they have weeks, not months. He confronts Voss about the pod; she denies knowledge, too convincingly. Emotional beat: the sickening realization everyone lies.

chapters.title: Names We Were Never Given
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The children research the drowned city and learn the colony's founders erased its true name and origin. Their shared identity as 'colony kids' feels suddenly hollow. Emotional beat: grief for a heritage that was stolen before they were born.

chapters.title: The Second Whitlock
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The pod occupant revives: another clone, activated decades ago, who claims the original discovered the beacon's true purpose and was killed for it. He offers proof—in exchange for Dominic's silence about the children. Emotional beat: temptation of an ally who may be a trap.

chapters.title: Fracture Lines
chapters.summary: POV alternating Mara/Dominic. The colonists split: some want to signal one fleet for protection, others want to stay hidden. Voss pushes a vote to extend the lie indefinitely. Emotional beat: a community discovering belonging built on deception is brittle.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dream completes itself: the children see the original Whitlock's final moments—he hid the truth inside the dream itself, seeding it through the beacon into young minds. Emotional beat: awe that the dead found a way to speak.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The second clone is found dead—pod life-support cut. Evidence points to Dominic himself. Arrested by colony security, he watches the beacon flicker unattended. Emotional beat: betrayal and helplessness as the lie begins to fail.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. With Dominic detained, the council votes to keep broadcasting the lie and abandon the children's findings. Voss wins—but we glimpse her private terror that the original's killer is someone she protected. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of leadership.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Deep
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The children free Dominic via the flooded tunnels from their dream, navigating by memory alone. Above, both fleets' advance scouts arrive simultaneously—the beacon's deflection is failing. Emotional beat: courage of the young outpacing the caution of the old.

chapters.title: The Killer's Face
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the original's hidden message, Dominic identifies the murderer: the colony's beloved doctor, who killed the original to protect the lie because the truth would have doomed everyone. Confrontation in the beacon chamber. Emotional beat: pity entangled with fury.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Zero Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The truce expires as both fleets enter orbit. The doctor, cornered, threatens to destroy the beacon entirely. The children begin broadcasting the shared dream on all channels themselves. Emotional beat: desperate defiance.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic chooses truth over the lie: he merges the dream transmission with the beacon's signal, showing both fleets the drowned city, the pods, the stolen name. On every bridge in orbit, sailors see the same dream. Emotional beat: terrifying surrender of control.

chapters.title: The Fleets Answer
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Both fleets hold fire, shaken by recognition—their own ancestors are in the drowned city's records. Negotiations begin on the ice, brokered by the children who started it. The doctor surrenders. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: A Name Recovered
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The colonists restore the city's true name and teach it to their children. Dominic, offered command, instead trains Mara as the next beacon keeper—not of lies, but of memory. Emotional beat: belonging finally earned rather than assigned.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Vigil
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing. One year later, the beacon still shines, now broadcasting openly. Dominic visits the original's grave and, for the first time, speaks of 'my' memories without shame. Emotional beat: peace—an identity assembled from truth, loyalty, and choice.
